Problem Statement:
Kumar gives up pursuing sports and decides to open up a company for helping students ace interviews and get placed. After a few months of hard work he decides to expand the company .He builds N offices in a line numbered 1 2 3..N. Each office deals with a certain product and has a staff requirement of X[i] 1<=i<=N . The staff requirement is the minimum number of employees required for the offices to operate correctly. The initial arrangement of employees Is given by Y[i] 1<=i<=N. Kumar can do one of three things: 1)He can expand the number of people in office numbered x by y employees 2)He can fire y people from office numbered x 3)He can check if at least one office from office numbered X to office numbered Y is understaffed Help Kumar carry out these operations efficiently Note: The initial arrangement will always be less the required arrangement. If Kumar tries to fire say A people from an office containing B people where A>B , the number of employees in that office reduces to 0. 
Input Description:
The first line contains an integer N denoting the number of offices . The second line contains N integers : the contents of X : the staff requirement The third line contains N integers : the contents of Y : the initial arrangement of staff in the offices The fourth line contains a single integer Q : the no of actions kumar takes The next Q line can contains either of the following: 1 x y : Kumar increases the number of employees in office x by y 2 x y : Kumar fires y people from office numbered x 3 x y : Kumar wants to know if any office in the range [x,y] is understaffed 
Output Description:
For each type 3 event output in a single line either “Understaffed offices present” :if there is at least once office understaffed in the given range Or “All offices at full efficiency” if no office is understaffed in the given range Note: Print without quotes 
Sample Input:
4
2 2 2 2
1 1 1 1
3
1 1 1
3 1 1
3 2 4 
Sample Output:
All offices at full efficiency
Understaffed offices present 
Explanation:
Kumar increases the number of people in the first office by 1 So the number of employees in each office is given by : [2,1,1,1] He then checks the range [1,1] : all offices in this range satisfy the minimum requirement so the output is "All offices at full efficiency". In the range [2,4] however understaffed offices are present so the output is "Understaffed offices present"
